## Natural history notes

A small creeping warbler characterized by its bold black-and-white striping, thin slightly downcurved bill, and nuthatch-like habit of moving along tree trunks and branches. In Florida, it is found in hammocks, pine forests, cypress swamps, mangroves, wooded parks, forest edges, and other habitats with mature trees. It feeds mainly on insects, spiders, and other small arthropods, foraging by creeping over bark, limbs, and mossy surfaces while probing into crevices for prey.
